messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated pod crash rate detected in fleet-redwood-gpu-1 (us-west1). 18% error rate over 3m, majority showing CUDA illegal memory access / misaligned address traces. Auto-escalation to oncall.

miguel: Oncall here, looking. Which customers impacted? :eyes:

ops-bot: Affected routes: /generate (hosted), some dedicated pools. Top affected customer: acct-omega (10% of traffic). Autoscaler logs show node flapping + multiple OOM/container restarts.

miguel: Pulling recent logs now. Anyone see a kernel oops snippet?

kevin: Pasting one of the container logs: 
```
I0403 12:14:22.123456 1 cuda_runtime.cc:78] GPU-exec: illegal memory access at 0x7f9c1b2e0000
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  misaligned address during pagewalk: kernel->gpu_page_walk()  (addr=0x7f9c1b2e0000)
```

kevin: Also saw a kernel trace on the node: `BUG: kernel NULL pointer deref in page_walk()` and repeated device reset logs.

miguel: Ok looks like misaligned pagewalk during GPU pagewalk path. Could be race between hotpatch and migration or a kernel regression. Which kernel version are the nodes on?

ash: All nodes in that pool are on ubuntu-22.04/gke-kernel-5.15.0-87. I just checked node metadata.

eva: Observed sudden increase in page faults when sequence lengths spike (batching=dynamic), so may be correlated with very long requests triggering larger KV cache allocations.

miguel: Immediate mitigation options: 1) drain affected nodes and force workloads to fallback to CPU or different region, 2) roll back recent kernel or runtime hotpatch if any, 3) enable conservative batching/disable continuous batching for the fleet. Thoughts?

sara: We had a hotpatch deployed 25m ago targeting small scheduling bug. It touched NV driver reload path. I can rollback that patch now.

kevin: Draining nodes will cause short term capacity loss, but we can spin up gpu nodes in a different pool with older kernel and redirect traffic. Can do gradual shift.

miguel: Start rollback of hotpatch (sara). Also start cordon+drain of 3 nodes with most crashes (kevin). Add canary route to fallback model variant (cpu-compat) for acct-omega.

ops-bot: Runbook step executed: `kubectl cordon gpu-01 && kubectl drain gpu-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (kevin)

kevin: Done for gpu-01 and gpu-02. Drain in progress for gpu-03. I've spun up 4 nodes in pool gpu-legacy-5.10 as standby.

sara: Hotpatch rollback started: reverting kpatch units across fleet. Monitoring driver reload logs.

miguel: Please capture kernel oops and dmesg output for a drained node before it reboots. We need an artifact for SRE/Kernel team.

kevin: Attached excerpt from /var/log/dmesg: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: failed pagewalk, address misaligned 0x7f9c1b2e0000
[ 1234.567915] BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request at address 7f9c1b2e0000
[ 1234.567920] RIP: 0010:gpu_page_walk+0x2f/0x120
```

ash: I also grabbed `nvidia-bug-report` output and uploaded to /tmp/incident-2140323000/nvrm.tar.gz.

miguel: Good. Next: notify customer success and affected accounts. Sara, can you draft a short notice with impact and preliminary mitigation? Keep it conservative: degraded latency and intermittent errors for generation endpoints, possible retries required.

sara: Draft ready: "We've detected GPU node instability causing intermittent generation failures and increased latencies for some customers. We're rolling back a recent runtime patch and shifting traffic to legacy nodes while we investigate. No data exfiltration suspected. We'll update in 30m." Want me to send?

miguel: Send. Also open a ticket to kernel team with logs and nvrm bundle, assign to @ash for triage.

ash: Ack. Ticket created: KERN-1429. Adding kernel traces + steps to reproduce (approx).

ops-bot: Autoscaling note: fallback pool gpu-legacy-5.10 currently at 40% capacity after warmup. Request throttling enabled for acct-omega to limit retries.

kevin: After rollback completed, crash rate dropped from 18% -> 3% in 12 minutes. Some residual restarts from already-impacted containers.

miguel: Good sign. Keep drains until stability holds for 30m. Also disable continuous batching for the /generate route to reduce large pagewalks. Rafael, can infra config that? (Rafael not in thread, pinged in separate message).

eva: Saw two containers still OOM'ing after rollback. Logs show allocation spikes then segfault in GPU runtime. Might be corrupted state during reset; re-creating pods clears them.

miguel: Ok, schedule rolling restart for remaining pods on affected nodes. Use `kubectl rollout restart ds/gpu-runtime` with maxUnavailable=1.

ops-bot: Action executed: rolling restart initiated.

sara: Customer update sent. CS responded they saw ~6% request error rate affecting a small subset of power-users. They asked about SLA credit.

miguel: Mark incident as P1 for now due to customer impact and node flapping. Keep timeline and collect metrics for postmortem. We should also add a guard in runtime to detect misaligned pagewalks and fallback to CPU before crash — file a follow-up with eng-runtime.

ash: Assigned follow-up: RUNTIME-847 add alignment checks + graceful fallback.

kevin: Drains complete. Crash rate stable at ~1.2%. I'll keep the legacy pool running for 2h and then we can progressively move back.

miguel: Great work team. Will start incident postmortem doc after 60m of stability. For now: priority actions captured, kernel team looped, CS notified, rollback successful. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: P1 declared. Postmortem owner: miguel. Next update scheduled in 30m.
